title: lagoon-scrub-notes-amira-2028-09-02
content:
Quick scratchpad from overnight on-call (lagoon rotation). Mostly freeform: timeline, immediate actions, followups and ideas. Use this to seed a short post-incident checklist and runbook edits.

Summary:
- Pager at 02:13 UTC: high 5xx rate from hosted API edge nodes in us-west-2 (elastic autoscaler flapping + a handful of auth errors).
- Impact: brief elevated error rate (~12 minutes) for ~8% of requests in the tiered-api-prod route. Most requests retried successfully by client-side backoff.
- Root-cause hypothesis (initial): transient cache invalidation + NLB connection churn causing a small window of 502/503 responses; autoscaler reacted to CPU spikes by terminating warm agents too quickly (scale-down cooldown too low).

Timeline (no frills):
- 02:10 UTC - received synthetic alert: 5xx > 5% for 3m (route: tiered-api-prod). Started console.
- 02:13 UTC - Pager fired to rotation (me). Slack #prod-alerts posted with initial context.
- 02:14 UTC - Confirmation in metrics: spike in backend latency and connection errors to model-hosting pool (m-host-pool-a).
- 02:16 UTC - Deployed temporary scaling cap: set min-instances=6 for m-host-pool-a to prevent immediate scale-to-zero while investigating.
- 02:20 UTC - Identified NLB target registration lag on a subset of instances: health-check flaps during redeploy cycles.
- 02:25 UTC - Rolled back a recent config change in autoscaler (PR #678) that changed cool-down from 300s to 90s (likely too aggressive). Rollback applied; monitored.
- 02:33 UTC - 5xx rates trending down; small number of auth failures persisted.
- 02:38 UTC - Notified oncall-leads; started a short postmortem doc stub (linked).
- 02:46 UTC - Incident declared resolved; kept min-instances=4 for 30m as precaution.

Immediate actions taken (commands / short notes):
- kubectl patch hpa m-host-pool-a --patch '{\"spec\":{\"minReplicas\":6}}' (temporary)
- reverted autoscaler deploy: kubectl rollout undo deploy/autoscaler-controller -n infra --to-revision=23 (PR #678 revert)
- captured snapshots: cloudwatch group: /redwood/ingress/tiered-api-prod (02:10-02:50) and m-host-pool-a logs (filtered for `health check failed`)
- short-term monitoring: created dashboard snapshot and invited Theo + Maya for review (link in linked_artifacts)

Runbook TODOs (original runbook gaps discovered):
- [ ] Add explicit rollback play for autoscaler-config changes (current runbook assumes safe defaults; missed doc for cooldown change). Owner: Theo. Target: 2028-09-07.
- [ ] Add step to temporarily pin minReplicas for model hosting pools when health-check flaps occur (document threshold: >5% target fails for 2m). Owner: Amira. Target: 2028-09-05.
- [ ] Update health-check tuning section: NLB health-check timeout vs app readiness probe misalignment. Owner: Maya. Target: 2028-09-06.
- [ ] Add quick grep commands to runbook for auth-error correlation (where to look for KMS/HSM latencies). Owner: SRE-runbook-owners. Target: 2028-09-08.

Followups and tickets to open (quick):
- Create RWINF ticket: "Investigate autoscaler cooldown regression and CI gating for config changes" -> RWINF-3421 (linked). Assign to infra-team. Priority: P2.
- Create ticket: "NLB health check vs readiness probe misalignment - propose safe defaults" -> link back to runbook. Assign to platform-eng.
- Chat with product/ops about impact window and customer-facing blurb (short timeline) - owner: Maya to draft.

Observations and loose hypotheses:
- The autoscaler config PR (#678) lowered cooldown to 90s to enable faster downscaling during low-usage windows. That change is reasonable for cost but unsafe for pools with slow readiness or long model load times.
- There was a small correlated increase in auth failures (401) for a subset of requests — possibly due to a short spike in KMS latency when many tokens were refreshed at once. Need to correlate with KMS metrics.
- Our existing canary gating for infra config changes seems insufficient; we should add a small slow-roll and an automatic traffic shadowing step for autoscaler changes.

Quick troubleshooting notes for next on-call (copyable):
- Metrics to check: /ingress/5xx-rate, m-host-pool-a CPU/ready, NLB target weight/registrations, KMS request latency 95/99th.
- Quick commands: kubectl get hpa,mhosts -n inference; aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn <arn> --output table; tail -n 200 m-host-pool-a | grep "health check failed".
- Rollback autoscaler: kubectl rollout undo deploy/autoscaler-controller -n infra --to-revision=<previous>

Automation ideas (brain dump):
- Protect autoscaler cooldown changes with a pre-merge check: if modified, require an infra-runbook-update PR that includes a simulated load test (CI job).
- Add a short-lived synthetic that exercises model load repeatedly after scale events to detect delayed readiness and trigger scaling hold.
- Anomaly detection on auth error spikes correlated to KMS latencies — if KMS p99 > X ms, throttle token refresh batches.

Loose notes to self (very rough):
- Did I capture the right window for snapshots? double-check cloudwatch export at 02:09-02:40.
- Remind Theo to add a short blameless writeup for the rotation notes channel tomorrow morning.
- Keep the temporary minReplicas change only until 09/02 03:30 UTC unless infra team requests extension.

Unresolved questions:
- Why did the NLB register/unregister on healthy instances? Is there throttling on the control plane side during redeploys? Could be tied to too-fast kill of warm agents.
- Are there any outstanding PRs that changed readiness probe behavior recently? (search PRs touching readiness handlers).

End of scratchpad. Will turn this into a short incident stub and raise the followup tickets after breakfast. If anyone needs the raw logs I pulled, I put them in /tmp/amira-lagoon-snapshots-20280902.tar.gz on my laptop; will upload to the incident folder when I get to my desk.
